5- Relationships: it is covered at its terminal part by the serous pericardium. The suprapericardial part is related: - In front: the thymus (or its vestiges), the pleura, the first two costal cartilages and the sternum. - Behind: right lung, the termination of the azygos vein. - On the right: the right mediastinal pleura and the mediastinal surface of the right lung, the right phrenic nerve. - On the left: the ascending aorta. The pericardial portion is related: - In front with the right auricle - On the left: the aorta 6- Affluent vein A single constant tributary vein is the azygos vein which ends at the posterior surface of the superior vena cava.

headers: Venous blood is returned from the body to the right heart by three venous trunks: - The coronary sinus which drains venous blood from the heart to the right atrium of the heart. - The superior vena cava (SVC) draining venous blood from the supradiaphragmatic part of the body (head, neck, thorax and upper limbs) towards the right atrium of the heart. - The inferior vena cava (IVC) drains venous blood from the subdiaphragmatic part of the body (abdomen, pelvis and lower limbs) to the right atrium of the heart. -The azygos system forms an anastomotic system between the superior and inferior vena cavae. It includes: - on the right: the azygos vein (large azygos vein). - on the left: the hemi-azygos (the lower hemi-azygos or small inferior azygos), and the accessory hemi-azygos (the superior hemi-azygos vein or small superior azygos). The azygos system primarily drains the posterior wall of the thorax. The superior vena cava (SVC)
rows: 1- Origin: it arises at the posterior surface of the 1st right costal cartilage by the meeting of the two right and left brachiocephalic veins. Branches of origin of the superior vena cava

- The right brachiocephalic vein It is formed by the union of the right internal jugular and right subclavian veins, behind the sternoclavicular joint. It is 3 cm long and descends vertically downward to the left. - The left brachiocephalic vein It is formed by the union of the left internal jugular and left subclavian veins behind the sternoclavicular joint. It is 5 cm long, it descends almost horizontally at the bottom and to the right to merge with its counterpart. 2- Path: it descends vertically along the right edge of the sternum

headers: Superior vena cava (OTT) SVC tributaries The inferior vena cava (IVC) 1- Origin: It arises from the meeting of the two common iliac veins right and left, in front and to the right of the fifth lumbar vertebra (lumbar). Branches of origin of the inferior vena cava The two common iliac veins, each results from the union of the iliac veins external and internal (hypogastric). The right common iliac vein is shorter and more vertical than the left. The common iliac veins do not have valves. - the external iliac vein follows the femoral vein at the level of the femoral arch and rises inside the psoas to unite with the hypogastric. - the internal iliac (hypogastric) vein is short and large, it drains all the satellite veins from the branches of the hypogastric artery.

2- Path: it rises vertically along the right side of the spine and the right edge, reaches the diaphragmatic orifice located in the tendon center and enters the thorax. 3- Termination: intra-thoracic in the lower wall of the right atrium, it is equipped with a Eustachian valve. 4- Dimensions: length on average 22 cm, caliber is unequal at its end is 3 cm. 5- Relations: The inferior vena cava is almost entirely located in the abdomen (in the retroperitoneal space with the aorta), except for a very small portion which is intrathoracic. In the abdominal cavity: - posteriorly: the psoas muscle, the right side of the spine, the right pillar of the diaphragm - anteriorly: it is related to the mesentery, the duodenum, the head of the pancreas, the liver, the right testicular artery (in men) or the right ovarian artery (in women). - on the left: the aorta and the right pillar of the diaphragm. - on the right: the ascending colon, the ureter and the right kidney. In the thoracic cavity it is covered by the serous pericardium. 6- Affluent veins: Above the liver:

rows: The azygos vein 1- Origin: in the thorax at the height of the 11th right intercostal space by the meeting of two roots - the lateral root is formed by the fusion of the right ascending lumbar vein (result of the anastomosis of the 5 right lumbar veins) and the 12th intercostal vein. - the medial root: inconstant arises from the posterior surface of the inferior vena cava. These veins penetrate the thorax by passing between the two bundles of the right pillar of the diaphragm. 2- Path: it rises on the anterior face of the spine to the right of the median line up to the height of the 4th thoracic vertebra. 3- Termination: at the height of the 4th thoracic vertebra (T4), it curves forward above the pulmonary pedicle forming a crook to end in the posterior wall of the superior vena cava. 4- Dimensions Length 20 to 25 cm in adults.
